program.title: Cricket Batter S&C Intro Block

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Beginner cricket batter, 1 session/week, 60 min, full gym access. No injury history. Moderate stress, 7h sleep. Ready for foundational strength and batting-support movement.
primary_constraints: 1 session per week limits volume; prioritize quality and transfer.
Beginner level requires stable patterns before intensity.
Monday-only schedule demands efficient, complete sessions.
sport_demands: Batting requires thoracic rotation, trunk stability, hip drive, and deceleration control.
Fielding demands hip/ankle mobility, lateral reactivity, and safe stopping mechanics.
Match endurance requires aerobic base and calf/hamstring/adductor capacity.
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Build repeatable strength patterns (squat, hinge, push, pull, carry, core) that support batting stance stability, hip mobility, and basic acceleration/deceleration. Use low-soreness accessory work to avoid interference with cricket practice.

workouts.title: Batting Setup, Stability & Hip Mobility
sport_transfer: Stable shoulder and trunk position translates to controlled bat setup and head position during batting.
Anti-rotation strength supports rotational power generation without trunk collapse.
Hip mobility enables comfortable stance depth and weight transfer in drives.
workouts.why_this_session: Build foundational strength patterns and mobility that support batting stance, reduce injury risk, and enable explosive hip drive. Activate stabilizers before any cricket-specific power work.

warmup.name: Band Pull-Apart
warmup.purpose: Activate posterior shoulders and scapulae; reinforce upright posture for batting setup.
warmup.load_guidance: Light band tension; focus on shoulder blade movement, not load.

warmup.name: Bird Dog
warmup.purpose: Activate core and reinforce spinal stability before loaded work; prepare for anti-rotation drills.

warmup.name: Adductor Rockback
warmup.purpose: Open inner thigh and hips for batting stance comfort; prepare for lateral movement in fielding.

main_work.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
main_work.purpose: Beginner horizontal press to build shoulder stability and chest endurance; floor limits depth and reduces shoulder stress.
main_work.load_guidance: Choose load so last 1-2 reps feel RPE 5-6; upper arms start on floor, forearms vertical.

main_work.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
main_work.purpose: Unilateral horizontal pull to strengthen back and resist trunk rotation; builds anti-rotation endurance.
main_work.load_guidance: Choose load so RPE 5-6; support hand under shoulder, spine long, no twist.

main_work.name: Pallof Press Iso Hold
main_work.purpose: Isometric anti-rotation under lateral cable pull; develops trunk stiffness needed to generate bat speed without collapse.
main_work.load_guidance: Start with light cable load; focus on breathing and steady position, not load magnitude.

main_work.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
main_work.purpose: Lateral deltoid hypertrophy and shoulder stability; supports balanced shoulder development for batting and fielding.
main_work.load_guidance: Choose light load; control neck tension; slight elbow bend throughout.

cooldown.name: Dead Bug
cooldown.purpose: Supine anti-extension drill to reinforce core control and lower back safety in extended position.

cooldown.name: Inchworm Walkout
cooldown.purpose: Dynamic posterior-chain and shoulder mobility; cool down with active movement and breathing.

injury_modifications: If shoulder pain occurs during floor press, reduce ROM by placing a pad under upper arms or regress to bodyweight wall push.
If wrist discomfort in dumbbell rows, use neutral grip or reduce load; monitor bench hand position.
If cable chop discomfort, reduce load and cable height; ensure tall half-kneeling posture and avoid pelvic shift.

weeks.progression_rule: Complete all sets with stable form; adjust load so RPE 4-6 on main lifts. Mobility drills should feel mobility gains, not fatigue. No pain escalation allowed.

program.nutrition_focus: Support consistent training attendance and recovery: adequate protein at meals, hydrate for gym sessions, avoid heavy meals <2h before training. Log water intake during cricket practice.
recovery_focus: 7h sleep baseline is healthy; protect sleep quality by avoiding screens 30min before bed.
Moderate stress: use low-intensity walks or cricket fielding drills on rest days to decompress.
Monitor soreness in first 48h post-session; if DOMS is high, reduce next session load by ~10%.
Daily 2-3 minute mobility snacks for hip and shoulder in sitting breaks.
safety_notes: Beginner: do not use max loads. RPE 5-6 is appropriate for learning form and detecting pain early.
No ballistic or plyometric work until movement quality is consistent across 3-4 weeks and pain is absent.
Prioritize cricket practice scheduling and do not train hard gym on match day or heavy bowling days.
Pain is a stop signal: if any joint pain escalates during or after this session, regress load immediately and inform coach.
assumptions: Athlete can access dumbbells, barbell, cable machine, and a bench or floor mat during gym session.
Cricket practice is separate from gym session; total weekly training is 1 gym session + cricket practice volume.
Athlete has access to coached cricket training and can report pain or fatigue trends.
Load selection and form checks are done with coach or experienced training partner; no solo max attempts.
First block is 1 week of assessment; progression to higher intensity/volume depends on pain-free completion and form stability.
